FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Backing needs a body twist to the rear window with slow reversing, while exiting only needs a scan for cars, bikes, and walkers before the door swings [A01].
Why it matters: group backing-exiting; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F01, sec10-F05 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
Curb parking hugs within one foot on the flat, while hill parking with a curb angles wheels left uphill and right downhill [A01].
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F02, sec10-F03 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
Hills with a curb split wheel direction by grade, left up and right down, while hills without a curb always point wheels right [A01].
Why it matters: group hill-parking; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F03, sec10-F04 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
Two-way streets park right only, while one-way roads park either side [A01].
Why it matters: group parking-sides; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F02 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
Some bans name places like crosswalks and driveways, while others name distances like fifteen hydrant feet and twenty intersection feet [A01].
Why it matters: group parking-bans; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F06, sec10-F07 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
Scanning covers ahead, sides, and behind for missed risks, while headlights cover night and poor sight including wipers-on weather [A01].
Why it matters: group visibility-lights; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F08, sec10-F09 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A02
Low-beams serve towns, oncoming meetings, and close following inside two hundred feet, while high-beams serve open highway free of oncoming vehicles inside five hundred feet [A02].
Why it matters: group beams; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec10-F11 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A02
Oncoming glare wants edge glances without high-beam revenge, while fog wants low-beams with edge-marking steering and slower speed [A02].
Why it matters: group glare-fog; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F12, sec10-F13 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A02
Rain strikes slickest in the first half-hour of oil mixing, while snow demands full clearing before rolling and chains for grip [A02].
Why it matters: group rain-snow; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F14, sec10-F15 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A02
Slick sheets want gentle braking with rolling front tires, matching the hazard rule that doubles the normal gap [A02].
Why it matters: group slick-gaps; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F16, sec10-F10 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A02
The law defines aggression by harassing intent plus an offense, while the behavior list names the offenses from sign-running to shoulder passing [A02].
Why it matters: group aggression-law; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec10-F17, sec10-F18 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A02
Drivers answer aggressors with space and ignored noise, while courts answer convictions with ten days to six months of suspension [A02].
Why it matters: group aggression-response; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec10-F18, sec10-F19 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
